subject: Fit check + next step after discovery call
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@airture.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + next actions from today's discovery

Hi Sam — thanks again for carving out time today. Short recap from our call so we have a shared baseline: 

- Primary use case: real-time contextual search inside Airture's knowledge base (support docs + call transcripts) for customer-facing agents.
- Key success metrics: 90th percentile latency <150ms for short queries; cost target below $0.0015/token delivered; 99.9% availability for peak support hours.
- Data & security: Airture prefers VPC/private deployment or hosted with customer-owned KMS; retention policy is 30 days for cached prefixes.
- Timeline: pilot (POC) desired by end of Q1 2026; procurement & security review expected in December.

Next suggested steps: 
1) I'll send a concise one-pager with fit + ballpark pricing for a 3-month pilot.
2) Rishi can do a 30-min technical scoping session next week to validate latency and integration points.
3) If that looks good, we can get a formal SOW and procurement checklist to your procurement team.

I attached my one-page discovery notes for your reference (20251103-discovery-notes.pdf). Could you confirm whether procurement should be looped now or after scoping? Also curious — is the pilot budget already allocated or should I include a couple of pricing options?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Checking in — pilot fit & timing

Hi Sam — just bumping this in case it got buried. Quick question: is proceeding with a short pilot still a priority for Airture in the next 8–10 weeks? If priorities shifted, totally understand — a one-line update helps me decide next steps.

If it is still of interest, I'm happy to:
- Send a one-pager with two pricing options (pilot + scale).
- Book a 30-min technical sync with Rishi to lock latency/connectivity assumptions.

Would Wed or Thu next week work for a quick call?

Best,
Neha

P.S. I can share a short case study from a similar marketplace if that's helpful.
From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@airture.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Checking in — pilot fit & timing

Hi Neha — sorry for the delay and thanks for the follow-up. We had an internal reprioritization last week (pushed a couple of infra projects), so I didn't get a chance to respond.

Quick answers: 
- Pilot is still interesting but we need a rough cost estimate to show leadership before committing to scoping.
- Security will likely want an initial answers doc (SOC2 + KMS options) — can you send a short checklist?
- Procurement contact: procurement@airture.com (CC'ing them on the next message).

Could you send a one-pager and a very rough ballpark monthly cost for the pilot (assume 100k queries/month, median query length ~50 tokens)? If those numbers look sane, I'll loop procurement and we can set a 30-min call next week.

Thanks,
Sam Rivera
Head of Product, Airture Inc.
sam.rivera@airture.com

Subject: Re: Checking in — pilot fit & timing (one-pager + next steps)

Hi Sam — appreciate the update and thanks for looping procurement. Attached is a concise one-pager (redwood-one-pager.pdf) that covers: fit summary, two pilot pricing options, and a short security checklist (SOC 2 posture + KMS options). High-level pilot ballpark based on 100k queries/month and the latency targets we discussed: 

- Pilot Option A (Hosted with customer-managed KMS): ~$4,500/month — includes dedicated throughput for test windows, 30-day prefix caching, and basic observability.
- Pilot Option B (Dedicated pool, reserved capacity): ~$9,000/month — lower per-query unit cost, better tail latency guarantees, recommended if you plan to expand beyond pilot quickly.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Procurement reviews the one-pager and confirms any required legal/security attachments.
2) Rishi and I schedule a 30-minute technical scoping call (I quoted two windows below).
3) If procurement wants an SOW/PO, I can draft a pilot SOW after the scoping call.

Proposed scoping times (PT): Wed 26 Nov 10:00–10:30, Thu 27 Nov 14:00–14:30. If those don't work, share 2x windows and we'll adapt.

If helpful, Rishi — can you confirm the integration touchpoints we should be ready to discuss (API auth, prefix caching behavior, sample throughput tests)?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
